# Taxonomy of Grid-Based Logic Games

## I. Cell Marking/Shading Games
Games where the primary mechanic is determining which cells to shade or mark.

### A. Pure Shading
- Akari (light bulbs illuminate unshaded cells)
- Hitori (eliminate duplicate row/column entries)
- Kurodoko (shade cells to isolate white cells)
- Nurikabe (shade cells to form a connected white region)
- Nuritwin (shade cells to create two connected regions)

### B. Shading with Constraints
- Heyawake (shade cells with number/region constraints)
- Kurotto (shade cells around numbered cells)
- Norinori (shade cells in groups within regions)
- Nurimisaki (shade cells leaving white peninsulas)
- Shakashaka (shade triangular regions in cells)
- Yajilin (shade cells following directional clues)

### C. Shading and Counting
- Ripple Effect (shade cells in regions matching region numbers)
- Satogaeri (shade cells with distance-to-region constraints)
- Usowan (mark true/false statements about shaded cells)

## II. Polyomino Placement Games
Games where the primary mechanic is placing or identifying polyominoes.

### A. Polyomino Identification
- Evolomino (identify polyominoes of increasing size)
- Fillomino (fill grid with polyominoes matching size clues)
- LITS (place tetromino shapes in regions)
- Shikaku (partition grid into rectangles matching numbers)
- Suraromu (place and cover polyominoes)

### B. Chained/Stacked Polyominoes
- Chained Block (place connected block chains)
- Choco Banana (place curved polyomino chains)
- Double Choco (place two types of chained polyominoes)

### C. Block Assembly Variants
- Five Cells (identify five-cell groups with constraints)

## III. Path/Line Drawing Games
Games where the primary mechanic is drawing or tracing paths and loops.

### A. Complete Loop Games
- Dotchi-Loop (create separate loops with constraint markers)
- Hashiwokakero (connect numbered circles with lines)
- Masyu (draw loop through pearl/circle constraints)
- Mid-loop (draw loop avoiding midpoint constraints)
- Moon-or-Sun (draw loop through marked cells)
- Slitherlink (draw loop around grid edges)

### B. Path/Network Games
- Hebi (draw snake paths in grid)
- Juosan (connect numbered cells with non-intersecting paths)
- Nagareru (draw paths from numbered cells)
- Numberlink (connect matching number pairs with paths)
- Nurimeizu (create maze-like path structure)
- Pencils (trace pencil paths with constraints)

### C. Hybrid Path Games
- Sashigane (draw L-shaped paths from numbers)

## IV. Region & Constraint Games
Games where regions and numerical constraints are primary mechanics.

### A. Region-Based Deduction
- Makaro (regions with internal logic constraints)
- Nansuke (regions with number-based constraints)
- Sto-stone (regions with connectivity constraints)
- Tilepaint (identify hidden regions by painting)
- Yosenabe (divide grid into regions by type)

### B. Logic & Elimination
- Sudoku (place numbers eliminating duplicates)

## V. Hybrid/Multi-Mechanic Games
Games combining multiple mechanics from the categories above.

- Kuro (combines shading and path elements)

---

## Notes on Taxonomy Structure

This taxonomy uses **primary game mechanics** as the organizing principle:
- **Cell Marking** games focus on deciding cell states
- **Polyomino** games focus on shape placement
- **Path** games focus on line drawing
- **Region** games focus on area division and constraints

Some games (particularly in the Hybrid category) could reasonably fit multiple categories; they've been placed according to their dominant mechanic or defining characteristic.
